utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a number of administrative and other matters before you begin, Mr. Tapuskovic, your cross-examination. The first one relates to you, so you might as well rise. It relates to the conversation that you had asked us to enter into evidence, and we are considering marking it for identity. But before doing so, we'd like to find out, since the evidence didn't make it very clear, is this a note or a transcript, or what is it? Please don't make a long speech. Just let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a conversation that was taped in General Smith's office. General Nicolai was examined about this. There are certain things in that conversation that Nicolai confirmed. The only thing that's still not certain is who conducted the actual conversation. He denied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In what form is it? Is it in a transcript or a note or a letter? How is it contained?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was translated. We received a translation, and it was represented to be a conversation conducted from Mr. Smith's office. Following Mr. Nicolai's testimony, the only thing we didn't know was whether he actually talked through an interpreter or perhaps it was General Smith himself who talked. At any rate, this is something that occurred in General Smith's office previous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Docherty is not here, but there is absolutely no prejudice. We'll mark it for identification. The second matter relates to agreed facts, and this issue was raised at the Pre-Trial Conference on the 10th of January. During the conference, the parties were asked by me to meet and discuss the matter and report back to the Trial Chamber by Friday, 19th January. Today is the 1st of February. We haven't had any report from the parties. So, Mr. Tapuskovic and the Prosecution, you must get together and report by Wednesday of next week on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can inform you that we have met. We have received a new offer about that. There are a number of facts that I'm sure we can go through by the deadline set by the Chamber. However, bearing in mind all the evidence that we have so far heard in this trial, a number of problems crop up in this respect. I do, however, believe that we shall be able to agree on a lot of these facts that have been offered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The next matter is a scheduling matter. Tomorrow, Friday, we will sit as scheduled, but early next week the Trial Chamber will issue an order indicating how Fridays will be used. Some Fridays we intend to sit for the entire day, other Fridays for half the day, and some Fridays we will not sit at all. But that order will be issued early next week. The last matter relates to the witness's evidence in examination-in-chief, so I'm addressing you now, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you remember that I asked you how you would be able to identify from the holes the direction from which the shots came, and you answered that you were able to do that by stretching a cord or some thread from one hole to the other; and I further asked you what was there distinctive about the hole made by the bullet. And I'd like you to answer that again. What is the area that is peculiar or distinctive about a hole made by a bullet which makes you know the direction from which it came? Just concentrate on the hole. I'm clear about the evidence you gave concerning the use of a thread or a cord stretching from one hole to the other. I just want you to concentrate on the hole and perhaps any markings on it or anything resulting from the impact which would indicate to you the direction from which the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One thing I need to confirm at the beginning. At the outset you spoke about damage that occurred as a result of a projectile and then you mentioned a bullet. I will explain about the projectile first. The evidence I have given so far have been photographs of damage caused by a projectile which hit one side of the building. When the projectile hit that wall, I knew exactly what side it was, whether it was the east side, the west side, the north side or the south side of the building. So the projectile hit that part of the building. As a result of the explosion that occurred, damage was caused around the hole itself. The projectile tore through the wall and caused further damage inside. The same thing applies to the bullet, except the bullet did not explode. It created a small opening and then the bullet flew on. It tore a hole through another door, and then finally inside we found the cartridge. There was no other damage except for the entry hole so to speak. When you have a shell, it's easy. You can see exactly how an explosion occurs and how it causes damage to a wall. If the wall is facing east, then it's not logical for a hit to have arrived from that side but rather from the opposite side, from the west side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, I was asking you about the hole itself made by the bullet, whether there is anything about the hole resulting from the impact of the bullet which might tell you where it came from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This sheet of foil is split in half and then this goes into the room, into the inside of the room, which tells me that the bullet came from somewhere outside and then tore into the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the foil is split in half. Is there anything additional which might indicate the direction from which the bullet came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I had nothing else. That was all I established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I'm sorry to interrupt and maybe this is not the appropriate time, but I just want -- if I may just follow on two things that Your Honour raised at the beginning regarding administrative matters. The first is another matter that we discussed at the Pre-Trial Conference was the subject of intercepts and Your Honours pressed the Prosecution to try to seek agreement about authenticity and perhaps be able to therefore drop some witnesses. We have -- that's an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me finish this matter first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. I thought you had finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. A Judge wants to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, during your testimony yesterday, you also testified about a few shelling incidents, and you mentioned that there was a shelling of a bus and a shelling on a house. My question to you is the following: Were you able, during your investigation, to determine the nature of the projectile that had been fired at the bus and at the building; and more, specifically, were there mortar grenades or were they modified air bombs, as we have heard about in earlier testimonies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whenever I carried out an investigation, I would find remains of mortar shells, those that don't explode but rather just stay there. Whenever I found that, I was able to ascertain that those were shells. As for other projectiles or missiles, such as bullets or anti-aircraft machine-guns, when those were fired, there is no angle. If it's a fragmentation bullet, it splinters into pieces. So I just say it's a fragmentation bullet. I sent the remains for analysis, and I can say that it is a fragmentation bullet and not a mortar shell. When you have modified ones, there were rocket motors which I also saw whenever I arrived at the scene. We would call those missiles modified ones, and this was later confirmed by expert reports, because these remains would then be forwarded to experts for further analysis. I spoke yesterday about the difference - and I can tell the difference - between various types of bullets. This is the sort of information that I would share with the inspector by way of instructions, but it is not necessarily accurate. Sometimes 10 or 15 days later we would get the expert report, depending on the amount of time that an expert took to write a report, and the expert would sometimes say, "I sometimes had 120-millimetre shells, I thought they were 120-millimetre shells, when in actual fact they were 82-millimetre shells." However, the victims were killed by mortar shrapnel. Whether it was a 120-millimetre shell or an 82-millimetre shell was a matter of lesser consequence which was subsequently established and confirmed by the expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I appreciate what you have just told us. My question was, however, a bit more specific, because I wanted to know if you were able, during your investigations, to ascertain what kind of bomb had exploded on the incidents that you mentioned yesterday from the Geteova Street number 5 and from number 12, I believe it was, and on the bus. Can you -- if you can, verify or explain to the Court which kind of bomb hit those three targets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The case -- the incident that occurred at Geteova Street number 5, that sky-scraper was hit by a modified missile, a projectile. The incident at Geteova Street number 12, which occurred before the one at house number 5, a modified projectile -- a modified projectile exploded in front of the building against the ground. Then there was another one that hit a building and the bus was hit by a fragmentation bullet and pieces, remains, of this fragmentation bullet, shrapnel, were found inside the bus. So this is not a rifle bullet. Those were scattered bits from a fragmentation bullet, and what I established at the time was that most probably this came from an anti-aircraft machine-gun. That was submitted for analysis and then an expert probably wrote something up later on in relation to what happened with that bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I apologise again for jumping the gun. Your Honours had pressed us on the issue of intercepts at the pre-trial hearing. We have provided a list of all the intercepts to the Defence and ask if they could inform us which ones they agree to and which ones they dispute. There are a small number that was done for when one of the witnesses testify, but there are some that are outstanding. I wonder if Your Honours could set the same deadline for us to report to Your Honours with respect to the intercept so that we could just get that moving along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The same deadline is set, that is, next week, Wednesday. The Chamber expects, requires, a report on the matter of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The only other issue is, I understand from what Your Honours have said that we will be sitting tomorrow as scheduled. Do Your Honours know about next week, the 9th of February, Friday? Because we're already planning for next week's witnesses, so it would be helpful to know if we're going to be sitting that day or if it's going to be a half day or not a day, if Your Honours know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. We will let you know by tomorrow, yes. That's about next week, Friday. Now, Mr. Tapuskovic, you are to begin your cross-examination. The Prosecution spent about 6 hours and 40 minutes, by my reckoning in examination-in-chief. Of course, you're not obliged to spend that amount of time. And to avoid the Prosecutor jumping up every minute to say that you are misquoting the evidence, I would suggest that where you have a doubt about what was said in chief, that you make an inquiry of the witness to have it verified so that we can have accuracy. Of course, it's entirely a matter for you, otherwise, how the cross-examination is conducted. But I'm just dealing with this as a pragmatic matter that has arisen time and again in this trial. Please commence your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll respond briefly. I hope that during my cross-examination the Prosecutor will not have to object, since I have made an enormous effort about this. I believe they will not have to spring to their feet even once. There is one particular spot -- reference to the transcript. I copied that. I'll deal with that particular portion of the transcript in relation to a specific incident. I can also say that I have made a huge effort, and I will do my best. I have the right to use up as many as six hours, but I will be doing my best to perhaps use up no more than half a day. If it takes longer, I will have to go on for a little longer. I will make an enormous effort to do as you bid me and perhaps even wrap up by the beginning of the second session of today. One thing I wanted to ask you at the outset was something else. At the end, I will probably have time, I'll probably have plenty of time, and I hope to be able to wrap up my cross-examination today, at least according to my calculations. I wish to be granted several minutes to explain a certain problem. I would not like to be going into that now, but if I could please be given several minutes once my cross-examination is over to address this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. The Prosecutor will no doubt be happy to learn that he can conserve his energy. He will not have to jump up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My entire file in relation to this witness is what you see in my hands. There's nothing more. I'll only be asking things that are important to my client, above all, of course, as well as issues that might help the Chamber understand the situation with the indictment. The first question, this is an issue that was raised a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Witness, you were asked a while ago to say what shells were used to hit certain targets. Can you please tell me what shell was used to hit the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer that question for you. The building was hit by a modified projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first thing I would like to ask you is, how about artillery weapons, aircraft weapons, bullets, machine-guns, snipers? You don't really have any expert knowledge of those, do you? Nor do you know anything about calibres, about mortars, about weapons that were used in this conflict. You are no expert in the field; is that a fair assessment? Or are you saying quite the opposite, that you know a great deal about the weapons that were used? Which is the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it's not true that I don't know about them. It's also not true that I'm overly familiar. I can analyse traces caused by certainly projectiles. I can identify the projectiles behind certain traces and certain evidence found at the scene. My task is to record the traces, mark them, photograph them, sketch them, and send them for analysis, submit them for analysis. I was taught about ballistics at the course that I took, and that is quite sufficient for me to identify what caused the explosion, whether it was a modified projectile, whether it was from a gun, from a mortar or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to apologise in advance. I hope you don't hold that against me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It's the same thing as if you, for example, took a sewing course and you never managed to make a decent suit. Wouldn't that be an apt simile, sir? Did you ever fire an air bomb yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and thank God for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll get to that later on. You can confirm that as a member of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just notice that counsel has his microphone on while the witness is speaking, and I don't want the voice undistorted to come out. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We must be very sensitive to that. I have been chided several times, and your microphone must be off when you're not speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I'm an elderly person. It may happen again, but I can only promise to do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I confirm -- I suppose I'm allowed to say this, aren't I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Since this matter is very important since it relates to protective measures, I suggest that your assistant to your right be assigned the job of turning your mic off when you're not speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. That is very helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can confirm, as a member of the police, that the police were part of the combat units, because sometimes you were part of the operations conducted by the BH army. Might that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I conducted on-site investigations following an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you knew about the preparations for an offensive, the offensive that eventually was launched on the 15th and the 16th of June, 1995? Did you know about that, sir? Is that when it began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about all these bombs, all these incidents that you have spoken about for three days? Did all of these not occur in the summer months of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I provided the dates yesterday. It's all in my various reports, and yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were there not ongoing uninterrupted clashes between the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska at the time in those months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't know about those operations. I wasn't privy to that sort of information. I never went to the headquarters or to the front line. I was at the police station. I was the person in charge of on-site investigations. I would go there, and I really don't know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So as a policeman, an expert in on-site investigations, with expertise in the elements referring to mortars and other weaponry, you were involved within a team in investigations, and that was exclusively with people from the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not only people from the police. An investigating judge was there, directing the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was the investigating judge with you when this little girl was killed that was -- a 10-year-old girl was killed, the one that was mentioned often here? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I cannot remember exactly who was on the team. There were so many investigations for me to remember that. However, in all the reports you will find the list of officials involved in the investigation. Whether it was headed by the investigating judge or under the law, it was allowed for an inspector to do that from the security services centre, or from the KDZ. It's all on paper. And I cannot remember specifically this incident of the little girl being killed that you are mentioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That is very interesting. We have been listening to the Prosecutor for three days. I haven't seen almost no document signed by an investigating judge. How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not up to me to sign these documents. I just confirmed that these were appropriate CSB documents produced by the Minister of the Interior. However, why there were no documents signed by an investigating judge, it's not up to me to say. I confirmed that these were my documents; I confirmed their authenticity and their form.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I do appreciate that soldiers and high-ranking officers visited -- had not visited the scenes because they could have been shot at. But how is it possible that there was not a single military expert who has perfect knowledge about the area of weaponry attending the investigation? I never saw a single report compiled by a military expert about the use of the weapons that you have been testifying about for the past two or three days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably a question for the investigating judge directing the investigation. I know that I was appointed by an investigating judge, and the other members of the team were skilled enough. Whether there were any military experts on the team to determine the type of the weapons, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of your experience that you acquired over the years - you started in 1993 and then you went on in 1995 - my question is: In 1995, I'm particularly interested in the 28th of August, 1995, when the incident of Markale 2 took place, did you participate in the investigation as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Not a single one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about a single incident. I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the first one, Markale 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't conduct that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You were questioned yesterday about 65 ter document number 00139, page 1. I'm not going to show it to you, for the benefit of the witness. But do you remember the report in which you mentioned a bomb with a Nazi eagle and a swastika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that photograph and I took it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My first question would be as follows: When I ask this question, we might need to go into private session, but first I will ask you something else. You went on to say, and the Prosecutor didn't read that, and it reads: "A Nazi eagle and a swastika was also found with a production -- with a number of the grenade which was probably originating from the Second World War," and then you took a photograph of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why isn't my mic responding to -- it's gone off now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay now. The light is on. So I have to repeat it. I don't know if the witness has heard me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So the bomb with a Nazi eagle and a swastika and a serial number, and you said that this grenade had originated from the Second World War; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the photograph all of this is written. I said that there was a swastika; there was a symbol with wings and there was a serial number. I don't have this photograph in front of me, but I said that it most probably originates from World War II. I think that's what is written underneath the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you took the photograph; I understand that. But I couldn't find this photograph anywhere in the file, in order to look at it and see what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an integral part of my photo file of the shelling of the Pavle Goranin neighbourhood that we discussed yesterday. Ten shells landed, plus one modified projectile. That is the incident that I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about that incident as well. There was fierce shooting on that day. Was there any shooting by the BH army on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the police station, which is in close proximity, and I showed that yesterday. These shells, including this unexploded one, fell on the neighbourhood in the school yard. They hit the facade of the buildings and one of the residential buildings was hit. I remember clearly. I was there. I heard the detonations, but I heard that it was a quiet day. But I underwent a stress on that day. But whether there was any fighting elsewhere, I don't know. But there was no operation from this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As an expert in explosives and other things that you mentioned, how can you explain -- how could this bomb fly through the air at all? It came from World War II, and I don't know what kind of artillery weapon could have been used to fire it. Are you suggesting that it was fired by the assistance of a launcher or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were gun shells that were fired from guns. They weigh several kilogrammes, and I don't believe that they can be fired by a launcher. Two shells did not explode; one was found intact with clear symbols, and the second one ricochetted, flew over a number of metres and hit a house. It was so powerful that it could not have been launched from a launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you're suggesting that the army of Republika Srpska had guns from the Second World War?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not suggesting that. I'm just saying that these shells had these symbols on them. I didn't say that the guns were from World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So what could have been used to launch these projectiles in order for them to reach the specific location? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the calibre of the ammunition is the same, but maybe it is an outdated production. I just documented what I saw on the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since Belgrade and the whole of Serbia throughout the Second World War was being bombed, and there were a lot of unexploded bombs, are you suggesting that this bomb had been brought from somewhere in Serbia in order to be fired from a gun at Sarajevo? Is that what you are suggesting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just telling you that the fact is that at the place of the explosion I found this projectile and what I saw on it. I found it peculiar as well, but I had to photograph what I had seen. And I put that in my report. That's how it is. I'm not suggesting anything about what has been brought and from where. I just want to say what I -- that that is what I found and that is what I photographed. I'm not making any suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you answer this question: This photograph that is in the file - unfortunately I was not able to find it - was it shown in the media in Sarajevo and worldwide, thanks to your report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the basis for the allegations that were often put forward, that this kind of bomb could have been launched only by Serbian Nazis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know, and I don't want to discuss that. I did my job professionally. I photographed it. I made no suggestions whatsoever. There was a serial number on the projectile, plus the eagle and the swastika. Whether anyone else made use of that, I'm not going to go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I must make a direct suggestion to you because I have certain proof in that regard. You have planted this projectile. You brought it to the location and then you used it for propaganda purposes. And based on that, it was often written in newspapers that the Serbs were Nazis, using even bombs from the Second World War. It was absolutely impossible for it to come from the positions of the army of Republika Srpska. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. There is no reason for you to accuse me of planting it. You have no proof of that. In the photo file, there is a photograph which shows that the projectile ricochetted an asphalt surface and hit the corner of a building. You probably can find a witness statement who said that their house was hit, that there was a detonation, that there was an explosion, in which case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, just answer the question directly. It's a very serious accusation that has been put to you and you must answer it. The accusation is that you planted the projectile. Give us a direct answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I had not brought it. I just photographed the projectile that was found at that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Tapuskovic. [Interpretation] Witness, just a question which comes to mind while Defence counsel is putting questions to you about these bombs with Nazi insignia on them. According to your experience, are you able to determine how this bomb is -- the symbols that were on the bomb itself, had they been put there by the manufacturer or by the people who use it, do you think? Because sometimes pilots or the military are able to draw symbols on the bombs they use. So this is my question: Do you know how the bomb is? Is it a Second -- World War II bomb or not? Was the insignia put there by the manufacturer or by the users, do you think? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say that as soon as I saw this bomb, I can say that I had never seen anything like that before. I noticed that it was engraved by a machine, not by hand, which means that this serial number was embossed by a machine; also the swastika and all other symbols. And that was the first time I saw something like that. That is why I photographed it and sent it for further analysis by an expert. That was my first encounter with a projectile of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yesterday, during this witness's testimony, you requested him to explain -- and I wrote it down. He said as follows: "We did that." You asked him to answer the question what that meant, what did he mean by, "We did that," and he responded that they had conducted investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what you referring to, "We did that." If His Honour asked me if we conducted the investigation, we did that. There was always a team on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I remember quite clearly. You referred quite frequently to "We went there," "We did this" and "We did that," and I asked you, "Who constituted 'we'?" and you answered, "The team."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to offer to the Chamber document DD00377. That's a witness statement given by this witness on the 11th of March, 1997. I would like this statement to be shown to the witness. Page number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, just to ensure that we go into private session if the witness's statement is being shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. If the witness's name is there, then we have to go into private session. It's the witness's statement, so I presume his name is there, so we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will be asking you about the TV building incident. Can you please look at paragraph 5. You say that the incident occurred only 150 metres west of your police station. Is that not true, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the sentence. What about this being true or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that your police station was at a distance of 150 metres from the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say: "The incident occurred a mere 150 metres from my police station."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in reference to the incident described in the passage above, in the paragraph above.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Two paragraphs down the page, is that also not in reference to the TV building incident? "In this case, we didn't find any traces of rockets. There is a possibility that the projectile dropped its motor during the flight."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found traces on the roof. It's not that we found no traces of the rocket. We didn't find the rocket motors; that's what I was saying. You saw the photographs; you saw the explosion -- what the explosion was like. The experts stayed behind and looked for their evidence, any remaining bits. I found nothing at the time and that is why the documents reflect just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, we can say that nobody ever found those rocket motors. It's impossible to explain how the bomb ever reached the TV building. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say nobody ever found those. I didn't find those. The investigation carried on for several days pursuant to a decision by the investigating magistrate. He can have other people look for it. I photographed the situation as it was on the day I came there, and that's what was eventually entered in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm putting to you is this: You fired that rocket, or, at any rate, someone from your own team, in order to stage this, the intention being to mock justice, to laugh in the face of justice. I'm putting it to you that you misused your powers and that you personally or someone else from your team did this or brought this about. Can you answer that question, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is no, I didn't do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you another document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have answered no, that you didn't do this, but the question also related to that act being carried out by some other member of your team. Are you able to answer that as well? Did anybody else from your team carry out the act?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a document. The document that is the most reliable document before a court like this, because it's a document by the UN and by the UN observers. The document states clearly who fired that air bomb and where it was fired from. We have sufficient copies available for everyone. I can show this document to everyone and I can show it to the witness as well, because it was him personally or someone from that team who had fired a bomb at the TV building in Sarajevo. There's the B/C/S, and we have the English, too. I received this a long time ago. I was going to use it at a later stage, but I believe the Chamber should be familiar with this document this early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand you correctly. You say you have a document from the UN and the UN observers which show that the firing was done by him personally or by someone from his team; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Show the document to the Chamber, and show it to the prosecuting counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor is familiar with this document. They have known about it for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll take a minute to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you wish to do with this document, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to read to the witness about the fact that the projectile which hit the TV building had been fired from territory under the control of the BH army. The flight was a low one, and what happened eventually happened. After that, he ran over; he carried out an on-site investigation of something that he himself had caused. He conducted an on-site investigation to prove that the projectile had been fired by the Serbs, whereas --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want to put the statements in this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Witness, you have in front of you the report of the sector staff of the UN Military Observers; can you see that. It is sent by the UNMO staff, Sarajevo Sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: June 1995, can you see that, too, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on. "Prepared by Captain Hanson, Operations Officer." Can you see that, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Approved by Captain Second Class Allan, Deputy Commander." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "Subject: Special report about the impact of a projectile against the TV building." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next paragraph: "20092 OB June, one military observer of the UN who, when arriving at the PTT building, parked his vehicle in the lower area, the parking area, observed the following." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Heard and saw an outgoing projectile across the parking place and road from grid BP," and then he states the grid reference. "The place is in BH territory approximately 1.800 metres from the nearest confrontation line." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then: "Dust was seen and a low-flying projectile heading towards the TV building." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then: "The projectile was following a low trajectory, travelling directly from firing point to target, and hit the TV building on the northern side, facing the British Cymbelline building." I can't read that word. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not read any more. There are other issues being raised here that might be interesting. But what I'd lake to ask the witness now is:

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Having read the document, again, were you the ones who organised this whole thing, who staged this whole thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not the ones who organised this whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get an order to go there quickly and conduct an on-site investigation, just like you described to the Judges yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go anywhere quickly. I didn't run anywhere. I waited for the remaining members of the investigation team to arrive, and it wasn't before then that we set out to -- set out for the scene of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about this? Isn't this something that was shown by all TV stations worldwide, especially the people in Sarajevo, and what people talked about was yet another heinous crime by the Serbs, simply because a media building had been targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The journalists were probably just doing their job. I was doing mine. I had a lot on my plate that day. I conducted an on-site investigate, and I have no idea what the journalists later reported to the world. All I know is that there were journalists inside the TV building. Some of them were injured. As for what else they were doing, I don't know. I suppose they were doing their job, just as I was doing mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps that is why NATO later targeted the TV building in Belgrade. I won't be going into that. That would be speculation on my part. But in other words, based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, no comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you not only wrote --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I have to say this -- Your Honours, I have to say it: I'd be thrown out of the courtroom if I said anything like that in a Serbian court. Fortunately I am here now and I can confront the witness in no uncertain terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you lied in your report, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. There are photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have to object to this -- well, largely to this question. It seems to me that counsel has shown the witness a document prefaced on the fact that him and possibly members of his team fired this shell. And as Your Honours can see and as counsel knows, there is no such mention at all in this document about who fired this shell, let alone the witness or any member of his team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he is not saying that the lie is based on the document, derived from what is in the document. I'd agree with you if that was what he was saying. It seems to me that he is just putting to him that his testimony is false, and I believe he is entitled to do that. That is his case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, may I continue? I agree with that, of course. What I would say is that in the witness's report and in his narrative of the sketch, all the witness does and all the witness has done is determine the direction of fire. When I started off my examination-in-chief, the witness clearly stated that he was not able to determine the origin of fire. And it is my understanding that in his evidence he has never stated the origin of fire. And so it's incorrect, in my personal submission, for counsel to put to the witness that he is lying in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask Mr. Tapuskovic to clarify. When you say the witness is lying, in relation to what evidence does that relate?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on this document and everything else that was done during the on-site investigation, I am convinced that it was either him or someone close to him - and I'm going to demonstrate that in the latter part of my examination, that the witness stage-managed other things as well - I believe that either the witness or someone standing close to him fired this projectile and then ascribed this to the Serbian side, and I stand by this statement categorically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have put that to him and he has said no, so let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Not only that you did what I claim you had done, you did something even worse, and I'm going to tell you what it is. The body of your friend who was killed was brought by you -- I don't know where he was killed or how, in the fighting. I'm sorry for any lost life. But I put it to that you that you brought the dead body of your friend, with the help of someone else because you couldn't do it on your own, and placed it in the atrium or the room where you allegedly photographed him. Did you do that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this small amount of blood that was found on the scene where he was allegedly shot, did you smear that blood there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A pool -- a puddle of blood was found. I marked it with a number, I photographed it, and I sketched it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's not a puddle of blood at all. If a person gets killed, there should be much more blood. I put it to that you that it's not the blood that belongs to this person that was killed at that location. I'm putting it to you that you planted the blood traces there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going now to present another document to the witness. Can you please bear with me for a minute. It's one of his statements. May I just sit down for a second, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You claim that you had brought him into the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that I brought him into the building, and in any case, it wasn't me who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm not going to correct that. We have to go through the same procedure in order to present to the witness the statement dated the 24th of April, 2006. Can the witness just take a look at it in order for us to save time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Prosecutor, is there any need for caution here in relation to the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, if my friend is going to be showing the first page and any page with his name on there, I understand that we're in open session, so for that part of the examination, perhaps we can go into private session. I understand that maybe the monitor is not being broadcast, so in that respect, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness confirm that he signed this, what is on the table.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we in an open session or in a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the witness has to be shown page 2, and I believe he has it already. I'm just going to ask the witness one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you please look at the first, second, third, fourth paragraph. Here it is. "At least some of the -- at least one policemen was killed in the explosion at the TV building on the 28th of June, 1995, when he ran to the impact area before the war had exploded." How is it possible, when you have a bomb flying at a low velocity, seen by everyone, incapable of killing anyone, how is it possible for any person to run exactly to the place where the bomb is expected to land? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I made this statement in 2006; that's 11 years after the event. There was discussion about this immediately after the investigation. When this man was killed, I didn't even know that he was a policeman. I learned that only later. He was at the place where there was a parked bus. There's a photograph of a destroyed parked bus. That's the northern side of the atrium. According to the statements, and that's why I say here, the witness said that immediately prior to the explosion the policeman was close to the bus. When the grenade ricochetted, the policeman ran across the atrium by the place where the explosion took place in the staircase. And according to the marks on his back caused by the explosion, it indicates that he had his back turned to the place of explosion. Some witnesses claim that he was near the bus when the explosion took place, that he had been found at the staircase and then he was taken to the place where he was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said something completely different yesterday. You did not -- had not seen the policeman before he had been brought. You had not seen him running towards the place where the bomb was going to land. You told us a completely different story, and I must put it again to you: You are lying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you a minute ago that I made this statement in 2006, 11 years after the incident. It is only reasonable to expect that you heard stories and discussions in police stations that this man was a policeman. That's why I said that it was a policeman who was killed, and that is the person who I was referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I must say this directly to the witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that by stage-managing the shooting at the TV building and this fabrication with the body of his friends and everything that he did, you, sir, committed a war crime, number 1; and secondly, you are obstructing justice and misleading the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the light of what you did, I put it to you, and kindly answer me: You must be fully aware of how things were staged on Vase Miskina Street, in Markale -- in Markale 2; you must be fully aware and familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I didn't conduct an investigation on Markale 1 and Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, what counsel appears to me to be doing is making statements from the bench, evidence from the bench, as in Markale 1 being staged, for example. On what basis does he say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I mean, that's his case. He is entitled to put it. In fact, he has a duty to put it. Those are his instructions. I mean, he will bring evidence. If he doesn't bring the evidence, then it falls to the ground. But he must put his case, and that is his case. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when the witness was questioned -- correction, when Mr. Nicolai was questioned, in response to the Prosecutor's question, he replied that those were the bombs and he used the word "sow," s-o-w. I'm not exactly sure what kind of language I'm now talking, but everybody is familiar with that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness explain what the word "sow" means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sow is a female pig.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right, because that is a big pig that just causes damage and soils the place that it enters, but it cannot endanger anyone's life. It just makes the place dirty and that's all. Were these bombs exactly something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no contacts with the pig.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no doubt about that. But I put this to you: You planted dead bodies of people killed elsewhere in order to prove that these kinds of bombs can also kill; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to demonstrate to you that you were capable of doing that, I'm going now to move to this incident that was extensively being dealt with - that's a terrible tragedy - when this little girl was killed. Let us look at what you did in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For that purpose, I would kindly ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us see how you, as such a skilled police investigator, conducted this investigation. I have no other choice, although I'd rather not have these pictures shown. Although this is still being dubbed as a victim of the Serbian aggression, because I have a question in this respect. I would appreciate if we can see these two photographs that are a terrible story of a terrible plight of a little girl. That's P125, page 4, and I think it's 125, page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Didn't the Prosecutor show them?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's why I am saying that they have already been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I will allow them to be put on the screen for no longer than 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No longer than five seconds, Your Honour. There is no need for any longer time. And then I'm going to ask my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead, yes. It's not those.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the number here. P125 -- oh, here it is. That would be enough. Can we stop this. I'm also unable to look at this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you said that you took these pictures in the morgue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that it wasn't me who took these two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you did say that they were taken in the morgue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it wasn't me who took the photographs. And they were taken in the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's how I understand it. Is there a sofa in the morgue? Is it possible, really, that there is a sofa in the morgue? Does this not prove that this photograph was taken in a flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, by just looking at the photograph, this is no sofa; this is a concrete table on which bodies are dissected. There is an aerial view, as it were, of the body, and you can see a part of this concrete table used to dissect bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It may be my mistake, but I'll check that so we don't need to show the pictures again. What about these photographs, these positively horrific photographs? Did these not make the round of the world on that day and the following days? All the TV stations across the world were displaying these horrific images, saying that this child was a victim of the Serb aggression.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw the images myself at the time. I was, myself, truly shaken by the fact that I was a member of that nation. The reaction was particularly strong from the non-governmental organisations in Serbia who asked us to go down on other knees and do penance for other people's sins. Did you hear them repeating that by some sort of litany all the time, that we should bear the sins committed by someone else, even those committed by some other people belonging to our own nation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't -- in my submission, the commentary is in appropriate or unwarranted, I would submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we don't allow commentary. I thought it was a question. What is the question, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did he read in the papers, did he see on television, that we in Serbia were being asked all the time to repent, as should all those who were involved in the conflict, not just the Serbs? I'm asking him whether he read about this or saw this in Serbia at the time. If not, not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you read that in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to take a break now. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't find my way around the document back then, so I forgot to tender these into evidence as Defence exhibits. Those two, D00-0319, the statement, his statement, and DD00-0377, for those two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are those the statements that you just showed the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On what basis are you tendering them? The witness didn't confirm anything in the statements. You can put them in when you're presenting your case and you can bring somebody who can substantiate what is in the statement. But the witness didn't substantiate anything in it, he didn't acknowledge any of the propositions that you put as being derived from the statement, so as far as I'm concerned, they are not to be admitted. They must await the presentation of your case, or, indeed, some other Prosecution witness through whom they may properly be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, he denied his own statements, so at some point he must not have been telling the truth. He denied his own statements, allegations made in his own statements. He denied it. He said it wasn't true. He said he never said that. Therefore, that must be evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: His own statements are already in evidence, aren't they? We're not dealing with his statements. You're dealing with the UN documents, the two --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I would like to have that document marked for identification, for that document to be marked for identification. But I'm talking about his two statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a misunderstanding. I had the impression you were speaking about the UNMO document which you had asked the witness to read and on the basis of which you put certain questions. You want this to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the UNMO document will be marked for identification with the reference D31.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statements that I showed the witness, that is, DD00-0319 and DD00-0377, I tender those two into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would object to the tendering into evidence of these witness statements. Firstly, counsel has said that he has denied material in those statements. I am of the opinion that this has not been the case, firstly. Secondly, counsel can put propositions from those statements to the witness and the witness gives his evidence in court under oath, and typically those statements are not to be tendered into evidence. It's perfectly proper for counsel to confront the witness with what he has maintained in the statement, but those statements do not, in the Prosecution's submission, go into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are not with you, Mr. Prosecutor, in your submissions. It's the witness's statement and it's for the Chamber to make of it what we think. So we will have them tendered into evidence, and please give them a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness statement dated 11 March 1997 will become Exhibit D32, while the witness statement dated the 24th of April, 2006, will become Exhibit D33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might I ask that they be tendered under seal, since they will have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll be dropping a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you allege that the girl was killed by a piece of an air bomb that tore through a wall and into the room where this girl was. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the report says. The girl was lying in a cot, in a flat. I didn't photograph that, and I explained the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My question was clear. You conducted the on-site investigation, didn't you? In your report we find the claim that the bomb tore through the wall, killing this girl who was actually inside the flat. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote that in my report on the day I completed the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P124. This is a photograph showing the wall of that building. If possible, can we please zoom in as much as possible so that we may be able to see the actual impact of this piece of the air bomb. Can we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you say that the bomb tore through this wall; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote in my report that a girl had been killed by the projectile. It's not the entire bomb that tore through the wall; it was a piece a fragment of the bomb that did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just in order to avoid any misunderstanding, Witness, I must read to you -- read back to what you said on the 13th of January in this very courtroom. The page is 1213, and the line is 21 through 25. You say as follows: "I arrived with the team at the scene, and I inspected the scene. I found traces or evidence of an explosion which I marked with numbers. I photographed the evidence." You say you made -- put together an entire set of the photographs of the scene and the surrounding area, and you also sketched the scene, you made a sketch of the scene. This was a provisional sketch, a provisional report, whereas you appear to have completed the final version of the report upon your return to the police station. Is that right? That's what you said yesterday or two days ago; I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on 1236, page 1236, that page, lines 5 through 13, you were asked by the Prosecutor about this. You said you conducted a regular on-site investigation and took photographs, as usual, and that the actual victims were photographed by other members of the team. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is that there was no victim for me to photograph at the scene. Following approval from our boss, the actual victim of this incident was later photographed in the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you were the first to arrive on the scene, weren't you? You did not go into the room, did you, the room in which you say this young girl had been killed. You didn't even try to look at anything inside the room. Rather, you made some drawings outside in the street. Would that seem to be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment this occurred, I knew nothing to indicate that anybody had been killed. I did say that yesterday. When I arrived at the scene, I knew nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So this most dreadful horrific hair-raising event that occurred, you spent so much time making your drawings but you never bothered to find out that there was a victim, a little girl; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. To put it simply, I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You go on to state this. The reference is still the same. "In this specific case" - and that's when you arrived at the police station - "in this specific case, that was what my bosses had agreed to do." Do you agree that my reading of that was this: Did they agree -- or did they order you to, in fact, not go there at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You misunderstand me. When I say that my bosses agreed on something, what they agreed on was a different matter, about me leaving that area and going to the morgue, to avoid risking my life. Sarajevo was being shelled, shells were falling, so this job was done on my behalf by a colleague from the same department. Our bosses just sent us to different places in order to reduce the amount of actual footwork. It was one of my colleagues who did the job. He went to the morgue following approval from the bosses. I'm not talking about the bosses of this particular team. I'm talking about my boss in my department and his boss, too. They had agreed that we could do it like this. We reduced the footwork. We reduced the fuel that we used up; we didn't even have to use vehicles. So it was my colleague. And when I talked about our bosses agreeing, that was what it was in reference to. It wasn't anything to do with the on-site investigation or what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you were a lot more interested in saving up on your fuel. Is that what you're trying to suggest, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to save my hide. That's what I was trying to save.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Once it had been established that this child had lost her life, was anybody sent over to actually make a sketch inside the flat to see where the child was, to mark the evidence, to find the hole in the wall torn by this dreadful weapon? Did anybody go and do that? Wasn't that the fundamental thing to do when carrying out an on-site investigation and when you have a death, anybody's death, let alone the death of a 10-year-old girl?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go there because I had been told about this. Nobody told me to go there. Why wasn't this done? I don't know. I don't think there was anybody left in the flat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly what information you received before you went to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I was told was that some sort of a projectile had exploded and that people had been injured. I didn't know who been injured or how many. I did not know that anyone had actually been killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How soon after --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How soon after receiving that information did you arrive at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly now, but I know that we were waiting for our colleagues from the security services centre. They were in downtown Sarajevo. Once they arrived, we took off together. Up until that point in time, it was the police securing the scene to the extent that it could be done at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, give me an approximate time. Was it half an hour or an hour before you arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the exact time we got there is stated in the report, but it must have been over an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you arrived at the scene, you're telling counsel that you went to the street and started making markings on the street. You didn't go into the house to make any inquiry about the injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't arrive on my own. I never conducted an investigation alone. It wasn't part of my procedure to go into the house and actually interview any witnesses. This is something that was done by one of my colleagues. What I did was photograph the scene, inspect the scene of the explosion, and that's what I did. I didn't actually head into the house to ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So your colleagues -- some of your colleagues immediately went into the house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And I think they compiled their own reports about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Witness, could you, in extension of President Robinson's questions, tell us whether the hole that is shown on your photograph there actually went through the wall? It's a bit difficult to see, and this is why I, too, would have fancied that if you had taken a photograph from within, then we could have seen that there is a hole all the way through the wall and not just in the wall. But can you clarify as to whether the markings that you have made here on this photo was a hole that went through the wall, all the way through the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Frankly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, how is it possible that you don't know? How do you explain that? Did you go closer to look into this hole, to see whether it goes all through the wall, and if it endangered anyone's life? How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came there, I went from the place of the explosion. I had no information about casualties. I found blood-stains outside the building; therefore, I didn't have any information that there was any casualty in the building. Later on, my colleagues were given this information, and there is an official report to that effect, and I made these photographs as you see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That was not what I asked you. We saw your drawing. It was being shown by the Prosecution for more than an hour. What I'm asking you, Mr. Witness, is did you go closer to look into the wall, to see if it goes all the way through the wall? How is it possible that you didn't do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't check that. All I know is that the damage was caused by an impact of a projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I put it to you that you had been instructed to tell a lie, and you're lying again. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber at all how is it possible that in such a terrible incident involving a loss of life of a 10-year-old child, how is it possible at all that no one went into the building, into the flat, to see on the spot whether there was any blood there and primarily - primarily - whether there was a hole through the wall? You don't have this information and that is why you are making this up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just to remind you, Mr. Tapuskovic, that in answer to me, he did say that some of his colleagues went into the building, so it would be incorrect to put that no one went into the building. That is not his evidence anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was probably my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But even if they did go into the building and into the flat, how can you explain, then -- how is it possible that you have no photographs of that? Okay, the child was removed. But there was no photograph showing that there was a lot of blood. There must have been a lot of blood when this child was dying. No member of your team photographed the scene. You didn't show us any traces of blood. And most importantly, you didn't photograph anything in this case, that is, the interior, a photograph of the interior. Why did no one do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that my colleagues entered the building. I didn't say that they went into the flat. I don't know and I had no information about any child being killed. Most probably they also didn't have that information. Based on later information to the effect that this girl had been killed, they probably compiled their reports. I didn't enter the flat, and I didn't even know that I was supposed to go there and that there was anyone killed there. That was subsequently received information. Why my colleagues went and looked -- whether they looked for people who were in the flat. But I myself didn't go into the flat to photograph the scene, and that is what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But the photograph of this child was broadcast around the world in order to illustrate the atrocities committed by Serbian criminals; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Besides, you didn't do that on your own. You were just following orders of your bosses; is that true? And then they organised the whole thing in order to establish a link between this dead child and an air bomb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was doing my job and I explained in what way I was doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: By making your sketches, you conceded to be an instrument in this kind of manipulation. This is what I put to you. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are just claiming that without asking any question. You just now asked me the question. Well, my job, and I said that at the beginning of this testimony, was to make sketches and to fix the physical evidence. It wasn't up to me to claim anything, and my job was to record only what I saw on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that you had been ordered to do what you did; you knew very well what you saw, that the bomb didn't penetrate the wall. You knew very well, just like everybody else knew, that this little child was killed.
