utterances.text: Counsel for the Defence, in the beginning of his cross-examination, put to you on page 12, line 5 -- well, he asked you whether you, while you were in the police, conducted combat operations for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I want to ask you: From when you joined the police - and that is the 1st of January, 1993 - up until the conclusion of the war, did you conduct combat operations with the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd like to show Witness 138 a document that appears to be from the accused. And I have copies, both B/C/S and English, for Your Honours and counsel. Perhaps it could be put on the ELMO. Actually, for the moment it's okay. It's okay for the moment. I'll just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you have a document there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it allowed in re-examination to be showing a document that we have not seen so far? If that is standard procedure, I wish to know, because I might then ask questions about this again. But first I need to study it. How come a document like this is now being used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you should ask -- you should be questioning whether it is a matter arising from cross-examination. Might I ask, Mr. Sachdeva, what does this arise from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it arises out of the questions -- well, actually, out of the claims by counsel that the television tower was -- the incident at the television tower was caused by the ABiH. And this document is, in fact, on our exhibit list and thus counsel has had notice of this document for some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness 138, you have a document there in front of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And at the top of the document, can you confirm that it reads: "The SRK/Sarajevo-Romanija Corps IKM/forward command post. Strictly confidential." And it is dated the 30th of June, 1995. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. It says the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, forward command post, and the number. I have seen all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if you go to the bottom of the document, right at the very end, on the next page, do you see at the end there the name -- well, do you see it written there "Commander, Major General Dragomir Milosevic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well. I want to take you back to the first page, if you move back to the first page. And roughly -- well, it begins halfway down that page, halfway to three-quarters of the way down that page, there is a paragraph that starts: "The Serbian soldiers are displaying unprecedented heroism." Do you see that paragraph there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just going to read on: "The Serbian soldiers are displaying unprecedented heroism, not letting the enemy get closer to their homes and families. The Main Staff of the VRS/army Republika Srpska, Main Staff Commander, Commander Colonel General Ratko Mladic commended the heroism of units in the north-western part of the front. Numerous congratulations also arrived from unit commands and civilian government institutions. Our artillery forces are responding with precision to the Muslim artillery attacks. In one such response on the 28th of June, they hit the BH RTC/Radio-Television Centre, the centre of media lies against the just struggle of the Serbian people." Do you see that paragraph there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have been reading along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is, the reference there to the TV -- to the radio and television centre, is that the same installation that you went to on the 28th of June, 1995, to investigate a projectile attack on that installation? Is that the same one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-138 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one in Sarajevo, only one building, the Bosnia-Herzegovina TV building, and this was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd like to offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no need to respond to that, but as far as I can see there is no signature to be seen, no signature by Dragomir Milosevic. Just his name. And I think this should be made an exhibit because it does tell us a lot, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We won't stand in the way of its admission. It will only go to weight.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will be marked as Exhibit P152.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sachdeva. Witness, that concludes your testimony. Thank you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not my intention to tire the Chamber, and I'm not sure that I'm able really to explain it now, but I did ask, once the cross-examination is over, for the Chamber to hear me on an issue that really has nothing to do with the Chamber. If I may, it's about the conditions in which I work. It's about our Defence. It's about the fact that I'm being hamstrung in my attempt to do something that I had been telling you about. Maybe for you to make a ruling to admonish the BH government to do something about what I think is not necessary now. Can I explain that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. But if it is a matter on which you should be making a written submission, submitting a motion, then perhaps it would be better if you did that. Well, let me hear you quickly. You have four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quickly, Your Honours. It's not for you; it's something that I was supposed to deal with in cooperation with the Registry, but they showed no understanding. This is about documents that I will have to go and get because they're very precious. I asked to leave for Belgrade for two days to get those documents. It's a lot of documents and it's very confidential. I simply wouldn't have the courage to have it transported here in any other way but actually for myself to go and bring it back. I was told that I would not be allowed to do that. I'd be losing three DSAs here, but I don't care about that, and I will not be allowed to travel back to Belgrade and have my flight paid before September. Believe me, I don't care about any sort of monetary compensation. I think the Registry would probably be saving up about 300, 400 euros for my DSA. I'd pay for the flight myself. I just need to go there, get those documents myself. It's something precious to me. I will use it to show something important. My investigators will be taking delivery this coming Friday, yet the Registry is putting obstacles in my way. That, indeed, is the case. I'm offering here to be a mailman. I'm offering to be the mailman myself. And just about a single flight ticket, an obstacle is being laid in my way. I think that is really putting spikes in the wheels of our Defence. It is not a question of me being willing, but at least they should say -- if I go now, and let us avoid any further explanations. This is an unpleasant situation. I had to waste an hour or so of my time this morning explaining this. So that's an issue. And money is being saved, in actual fact. But I really don't know what we're talking about here. In Belgrade the opinion prevails that we lawyers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, matters, such as DSA, between yourself and the Registry are not normally matters in which the Trial Chamber will involve itself, unless there is an issue of a fair trial. I think you should seek to have the matter resolved in the first instance by pursuing representations with the Registry. The Trial Chamber would not involve itself in that matter at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have just said is prejudicial to our defence. I have no way of obtaining these documents in a matter of days. It might take between 10 and 15 days and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't you pay the 400 euros yourself and then make a claim on the Registry and see how that works.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I will do. But let me just tell you -- or perhaps I won't tell you what the reply was. I'll do that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is not coming from the Chamber, I should say. It's just a strategic approach that you might wish to follow. We're going to break now, Mr. Tapuskovic, because there is nothing more that the Chamber can do at this stage. We will resume tomorrow morning, at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
